newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bank raising capital by public offer.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bank raising capital by public offer.

text.p: Export Development Bank of Egypt said on Wednesday it was offering investors shares worth almost 60 million ($18 million) pounds to raise its paid-in capital to 250 million.
Bank officials said the share offering would cut the government's holding to about 75 percent from the current 98.52 percent.

The bank said investors could buy the 597,280 shares -- which have a par value of 100 pounds -- for 250 pounds a share. Bank officials said they would put the difference of 150 pounds per share, the amount which did not go into capital, into reserves.
The offer is open for 40 days from December 8 but the bank can close it on December 18 if it is covered.
Investors must pay an initial 63.75 pounds for every share they bid for, which represents a quarter of the share's actual value, in addition to 1.25 pounds handling fees.
The bank said the capital increase was aimed at raising more funds for its export-oriented activities.
The share offering is in line with the government's policy of privatisation, which includes reducing the state's stake in joint ventures between state banks and foreign banks.
The bank's public-sector shareholders had put in another 121.27 million pounds since September, on top of its original paid-in capital of 69 million.
The state has repeatedly said it will not privatise the four main retail banks but the cabinet announced the decision to sell part of Export Development Bank in September.
The export bank currently has 690,000 shares that rarely trade on the stock exchange.
In 1995/96 financial year ending June 30, the bank said it made a net after-tax profit of 37.09 million pounds. It forecast profits to rise to 80.89 million pounds in the current 1996/97 year.
